hero.badge: Real-time visual product detection in video
hero.title: Pause the video.
hero.subtitle: Find the product.
hero.description: Pause2Shop analyzes video and images, detects every garment, shoe, or accessory, and cross-references it against a proprietary fashion catalog and reverse visual search. With provenance and confidence behind every result.

howItWorks.title: How it works

step1.title: Pause
step1.description: Stop the video at the exact moment.

step2.title: Detect
step2.description: AI locates the products visible in the frame.

step3.title: Find
step3.description: Matching against the catalog and reverse visual search.

howItWorks.heading: Five steps between a frame and a product you can buy
howItWorks.description: The full pipeline runs per detected object, with a call budget and cache at every stage.

capture.title: Frame capture
capture.body: Candidate frames are pulled from the video (uploaded, YouTube, or screen) by FPS and scene-change detection. Near-identical frames are dropped via perceptual hash, so they never reach detection.

detect.title: Multimodal detection
detect.body: A vision model locates every object with a box, category, color, and relationship to the person (worn, held, background). Only the categories you chose are analyzed.

dedupe.title: Tracking and deduplication
dedupe.body: Objects keep their identity across frames and are merged globally: the same jacket reappearing ten times is a single product, with its best crop selected.

match.title: Catalog matching
match.body: Each crop is first searched against our own catalog in a cascade: exact hash → perceptual hash → visual embedding. If there's no strong enough match, it falls back to reverse visual search.

result.title: Result with provenance
result.body: Every result arrives with a score, the stage that resolved it, and its origin (catalog or external provider). Nothing is published below the configured confidence threshold.

useCases.title: Use cases
useCases.heading: Built for video catalogs, not a single photo

primary.title: VOD and on-demand video
primary.body: Turns a video catalog into a product catalog. The full video is analyzed, recurring items are deduplicated, and you get the product list with the timestamp where each appears.
primary.point1: Videos up to 2 minutes per job (configurable)
primary.point2: Timestamp and source frame per product
primary.point3: Call budget and cost per video

discovery.title: Product discovery
discovery.body: The user sees something on screen and wants to know what it is. One image is enough to start the search.

catalogMatch.title: Catalog matching
catalogMatch.body: Cross-references detections against your own catalog before reaching out to the web: more precision, lower cost.

visualShopping.title: Visual shopping
visualShopping.body: Buyable results with price, availability, and a direct link to the store's product page.

clientDemos.title: Client demos
clientDemos.body: Presentation mode, cost panel, and sample data ready to show without depending on credentials.

capabilities.title: Capabilities
capabilities.heading: Everything that already works, with a direct link to check it

video.body: Uploaded video, YouTube, or screen capture, with continuous analysis and a detection overlay on the player.

image.body: Upload an image and get the detected objects with their crops, ready to search.

connectors.title: Catalog connectors
connectors.body: Modular registry of fashion sources with real status: implemented, unverified, or pending a commercial agreement.

embeddings.title: Visual embeddings
embeddings.body: Local CLIP or a deterministic hash provider for demos. Full reindex from the admin panel whenever the model changes.

catalog.title: Normalized catalog
catalog.body: A single product schema with normalized brand and category, price history, multi-level dedup, and source traceability.

cost.title: Cost and budget
cost.body: Per-provider call counters, a cost cap per video, and caching so paid searches never repeat.

complianceNote.body: robots.txt checked before every request, Crawl-delay respected, an identifiable User-Agent with contact info, and zero anti-bot evasion. Sources that require a partner or affiliate agreement aren't ingested until it's in place.

callout.title: How to read this table
callout.body: Real status is the honest label: it only says verified if this source has real products in the catalog extracted by the pipeline — code existing isn't enough. Health is how the store responds right now, and extraction measures what percentage of listings were resolved without AI (with structured data or the DOM); AI is only the last resort. Live checks don't run automatically for every source: that would be discourteous to the stores.

storage.description: Backend chosen automatically based on whether a valid connection string is present.
storage.fileWarning: File mode: the catalog is persisted as JSON and vector search runs in memory. Configure a postgres:// connection string (Neon's -pooler endpoint) and run the migrations to enable pgvector.

embeddings.description: Changing providers changes the dimension: you need to reindex or the old vectors stop being comparable.
embeddings.hashWarning: hash provider: deterministic 64-dimension vectors for demos and tests. It doesn't do real visual similarity — install the local provider with npm run embeddings:install in catalog-scraper and set CATALOG_IMAGE_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=local.

matching.title: Matching and dedup thresholds
matching.description: Nothing is published below the minimum score: we'd rather return no result than a dubious one.

compliance.title: Ingestion limits and compliance
compliance.description: The defaults are deliberately conservative: it's better to take longer than to bother a store.
compliance.policyBody: {policy}. Also: Crawl-delay respected when a store declares it, an identifiable User-Agent with contact info, and a circuit breaker that backs off under sustained blocks. Sources requiring a partner or affiliate agreement aren't ingested until one is in place.

observability.title: Observability and cache
observability.logsValue: In-memory circular buffer (750 events) + structured JSON to stdout
observability.healthCacheValue: 10 minutes per source; live checking is manual
observability.footnote: All observable state belongs to the process: restarting the service resets counters and the log buffer. For real history, collect stdout and use the Postgres backend.

transportNote.title: Scope of these logs
transportNote.persistentBody: Events are persisted in the database: the console also shows the history of previous jobs. The SSE stream only delivers events from this invocation; the rest arrives via polling.
transportNote.ephemeralBody: No database is configured, so logs live in memory only and are lost when the process restarts. Set DATABASE_URL (a postgres:// string) and run npm run db:migrate to get history.
